newsitem.title: FRANCE: Europe "needs a gas directive" - France's Borotra.
newsitem.headline: Europe "needs a gas directive" - France's Borotra.

text.p: A European gas policy, governed by a European gas directive, is essential to safeguard the future development of the industry, French industry minister Franck Borotra said on Thursday.
Speaking at the gas executives summit conference, Borotra said that Europe's major concern is to safeguard security of supply, as it depends so heavily on imports.
But a common policy is essential as there are differing views between countries like France, which imports nearly all its gas, and those like Britain, which will soon be a net exporter.
"A European policy is essential," he said. "We need to avoid emerging competition taking us from a rigid system to an uncontrolled system which could threaten security of supply.

"We need a directive. France wants to approach deregulation in a different way from the U.S. or U.K. Our approach would avoid all dogma while at the same time we would not automatically defend the status quo."

In particular Barotra wanted to see some consumers continue to be able to buy gas at subsidised prices. "Some customers should be allowed supplies at guaranteed costs, as such exemption from competition is vital to their own competitiveness."

The essential points behind the European gas market are deciding how open the open market should be, and working out how to define "eligible customers", those who should be exempted from the full force of competition. Borotra added that both power generation and use as a transport fuel will ensure the growth of gas demand. He said that France currently imports 20 bcm a year of liquefied natural gas and is looking to import in the future from Nigeria and Trinidad and Tobago.
